reports.authors: Song X; Lv J; Ge S; Xu S; Wu Y; Zheng Y; Zhou W; Li L; Zhang Y; Zhang J; Chen ZX; Gao P; Yin P; Yin J; Liu C

p.13-14 Methods 'Data source' and 'Assessment of physical activity and grouping'

reports.reviewer_notes: No screening disposition code in vocabulary_crosswalks.scope_stream.from_screening_disposition cleanly represents 'retained as background' (EXCLUDE_TA/EXCLUDE_FT map to 'excluded OR background if retained for context', with no distinct background-admission code). Left screening_decision_reviewer_A/B null rather than forcing EXCLUDE_FT, and recorded my own classification in eligibility_opinion instead. My opinion: this is a resting cross-sectional self-reported habitual-exercise (EX vs SED) comparison with NO identifiable single bout and no reported time-since-last-exercise control, so it cannot satisfy Core A (needs an identifiable bout, contract 2.1-2.2) or Support B (needs >=2 identified bouts with explicit bout-to-sample timing, contract 2.4); charted as background per contract 2.5 / manual 'resting cross-sectional training studies = background'.
reports.author_stated_use: Mechanistic/discovery framing: 'to construct a more holistic atlas of how regular exercise reshapes immunometabolic circuits' and '...to translate these insights into more precise and scalable health interventions' (Intro, p.1); Abstract frames results as providing 'a theoretical basis for enhancing public health and preventing chronic diseases'; Discussion explicitly proposes findings as 'candidate biomarkers and regulatory pathways that may inform prevention and management of chronic diseases' (p.12).
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.12 Discussion: 'the convergent enhancement of antigen presentation capacity across cMono and B cell subsets, coupled with the amplified APCs-T cell cross-talk, may collectively underlie the enhanced immune surveillance and reduced susceptibility to infection documented in physically active populations (5, 58)' - this concerns chronic/habitual-exercise immune enhancement, not an acute post-bout open-window/immunosuppression construct; the term 'open window' is not used anywhere in the text.

study_families.study_label: CIMA (Chinese Immune Multi-omics Atlas) natural cohort - exercise-habit substudy (regular exerciser EX vs sedentary SED)
study_families.design: Cross-sectional observational comparison of self-reported regular exercisers (EX) vs sedentary controls (SED) drawn from the CIMA natural cohort; single resting timepoint per participant; no identifiable acute exercise bout (p.2, p.13 Methods 'Data source').
study_families.training_load: EX defined as >=3 exercise sessions/week with >=150 min/week moderate-intensity OR >=75 min/week vigorous-intensity activity (WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour, ref 23); SED defined as self-reported zero exercise frequency AND zero exercise duration ('almost no exercise') with a predominantly sitting daily posture (Methods 'Assessment of physical activity and grouping', p.13).
study_families.study_notes: CIMA natural cohort n=428 Chinese adults (nonobese, BMI<30 kg/m2, aged 20-40y, no active infectious disease/cancer/chronic infectious disease/pregnancy at recruitment); 314 remained eligible after excluding incomplete physical-activity questionnaires; final analysis population n=86 (40 EX + 46 SED) after applying strict EX/SED criteria (Methods p.13; fig. S1A). BGI-IRB 21157-T3 ethics approval; written informed consent (p.13).

cohorts.cohort_label: CIMA cohort participants classified as regular exercisers (EX, n=40) or sedentary controls (SED, n=46); n=86 analyzed
cohorts.baseline_health: Generally healthy, nonobese (BMI<30 kg/m2) adults aged 20-40y; no active infectious disease, cancer or chronic infectious disease (e.g. tuberculosis) history, no pregnancy at recruitment; smoking/alcohol/sleep/diet recorded but not exclusionary (Methods 'Data source', p.13; fig. S1A).
cohorts.n_recruited: 428 (full CIMA natural cohort); 314 remained eligible after excluding participants with missing physical-activity questionnaire responses; 86 (40 EX + 46 SED) met the strict EX/SED criteria and were analyzed (Methods p.13).
cohorts.age_sex: n=86: weighted mean age 28.2y (95% CI 27.2-29.2); SED mean 28.9y (27.5-30.3), EX mean 27.4y (26.0-28.8); sex overall 28 male (32.6%)/58 female (67.4%); SED 9 male (19.6%)/37 female (80.4%); EX 19 male (47.5%)/21 female (52.5%) - SED group predominantly female, noted by authors as a potential confound addressed via sex-adjusted models and a female-restricted sensitivity analysis (fig. S1A; p.2, p.13 Limitations).
cohorts.training_status: EX = self-reported regular exercise meeting WHO volume/frequency thresholds (n=40); SED = self-reported zero exercise frequency/duration, sitting-dominant posture (n=46) (Methods p.13).
cohorts.sport: NR (specific exercise mode/sport type not reported; only intensity/frequency/duration categories from questionnaire, p.13-14).
cohorts.cohort_notes: Recruited at BGI Pengcheng Clinic health examinations, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, Nov 2021-Nov 2022 (Methods p.13). BMI overall 21.3+/-3.0 (SED 20.7+/-3.0, EX 22.0+/-2.9) (fig. S1A). Not all 86 participants have complete data across every omics modality (Methods p.13; table S1).
cohorts.age_range: Enrollment criterion: 20-40 years (Methods p.13, 'Data source'); analyzed n=86 weighted mean 28.2y (95% CI 27.2-29.2) (fig. S1A); explicit observed min-max age range NR.

report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: 40 EX + 46 SED analyzed in the multiomics integration; platform-specific analyzed n is lower for several assays (see sample_sets; table S1 '1.2 sample_omics', opened from the supplementary tables zip for this extraction).
report_cohort_links.link_notes: No identifiable single exercise bout; cross-sectional self-reported habitual-exercise classification; charted as background per contract 2.5 / manual (resting cross-sectional training-habit comparison). 'Time since last exercise' before blood draw is NOT reported for either group.

sample_sets.intervention_phase: NA (cross-sectional habitual-exercise classification; no training intervention phase).
sample_sets.exercise_mode: NR (specific exercise mode/sport type not reported; only self-reported intensity/frequency/duration categories, Methods p.13).
sample_sets.control: Between-group comparator design (EX vs SED, self-selected habitual exercise strata); no acute-exercise bout, no pre/post timing.
sample_sets.exercise_end_definition: NA - no identifiable bout; resting cross-sectional sample; exercise-cessation timing concept does not apply.
sample_sets.timepoint_as_reported: Single resting blood draw, fasting, collected in the morning; no exercise bout referenced; time since last exercise bout NOT reported for either group (Methods p.14 'Blood collection and PBMC separation').
sample_sets.assay_platform: scRNA-seq (Scanpy v1.10.3 pipeline; QC, normalization, Harmony batch correction, Louvain clustering)
sample_sets.n_cells: NR (aggregate total 1,317,665 cells for EX+SED combined; per-group split not reported, Fig.1D p.3)
sample_sets.repeated_sampling: None; single cross-sectional resting sample per participant, no repeated bouts or timepoints.
sample_sets.pairing_structure: Unpaired, independent groups (EX vs SED), not individually matched 1:1.
sample_sets.age_sex_stratum: EX: n=40 enrolled, 19M/21F, mean age 27.4y; SED: n=46 enrolled, 9M/37F, mean age 28.9y (fig. S1A); platform-specific analyzed n given in n_participants.
sample_sets.preanalytics: 10 mL whole blood in EDTA tubes; stored at 4C, processed within 4h; centrifuged 1600g/10min for plasma separation; cell fraction diluted in PBS+2%BSA, Ficoll density-gradient PBMC isolation; PBMC cryopreserved (90% FBS+10% DMSO, stepwise cooling, LN2 long-term storage); only samples with viability >80% used for library construction/sequencing (Methods 'Blood collection and PBMC separation', p.14).
sample_sets.circadian: Blood collected consistently in the morning hours under fasting conditions, over a 12-month recruitment window (Nov 2021-Nov 2022) (Methods 'Data source' p.13 and 'Blood collection and PBMC separation' p.14).
sample_sets.missing_data: scRNA-seq QC: 500-6000 genes/cell, 1000-25000 UMIs, mitochondrial content <10%; doublets removed via Scrublet (expected doublet rate 0.06) (Methods p.14). scATAC-seq QC: TSS enrichment >=10, nucleosome signal <4, blacklist ratio <0.05; exact unique-fragment count threshold reported ambiguously in the PDF text extraction ('1x10^5 and 1x10^5') - flagged UNCLEAR (Methods p.15).
sample_sets.cell_context: PBMC; computationally resolved into 6 major immune lineages (CD4+ T, CD8+ T, unconventional T, B, myeloid, NK) and 34 subsets (table S1 '1.5 curated level and marker').
sample_sets.sample_notes: 39/40 EX participants contributed usable scRNA-seq data (table S1 '1.2 sample_omics'; cross-tabulated against '1.1 sample_metadata' group column).
sample_sets.exercise_duration: NA - no identifiable single bout; habitual weekly duration recorded only as a categorical/derived cohort-level variable (see study_families.training_load), not a bout-level duration.
sample_sets.intensity_metric: NA - no bout; self-reported categorical habitual intensity (low/moderate/high/almost none) is a cohort-classification variable, not a sample-level bout intensity metric (Methods p.13).

precision_validation.evidence_notes: QC thresholds described for scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq and FDR correction applied (Methods p.14-16), but no technical-replicate ICC/CV is reported for this specific CD8-CTL signature; ATAC pseudobulk 'replicates' are computationally generated non-overlapping cell subsamples, not independent biological replicates.

Cross-sectional single resting timepoint; no identifiable exercise bout exists to anchor an organising-window time bin (sample_sets.time_bin=NA for this report); the 0-72h within-window framework does not apply to this chronic/habitual-exposure background design.
CD8+ CTL is a defined, marker-gene-annotated (GZMB/TBX21/EOMES) adaptive cytotoxic T-cell subset within a 17-subset CD8+/unconventional-T hierarchy (p.7).
No repeated-measures, within-person variability, or responder analysis design (cross-sectional between-group comparison only); individualization not examined for this marker.

Enhanced TF activity and up-regulated cytotoxic genes (GZMB/GZMA/PRF1) are interpreted as 'epigenetic preactivation of effector function' (p.7), but no direct ex vivo/in vitro cytotoxicity assay or clinical/infection outcome was measured; linkage is inferred from transcriptional/chromatin proxies only.

Single-cohort (CIMA) cross-sectional analysis; no independent replication cohort. A 'female-restricted sensitivity analysis' (figs. S11,S12) is an internal subgroup robustness check within the same cohort, not independent external validation (p.13).

Requires PBMC isolation plus paired scRNA-seq+scATAC-seq library prep/sequencing and a multi-tool bioinformatic pipeline (Scanpy/ArchR/SCENIC); authors do not report cost, turnaround time or field-deployability for this signature (not discussed in Limitations, p.13).
Promoter DAR for HLA-DQB1/HLA-DQA1 reported with FDR values (4.01e-52; 1.67e-08) (Fig.3H), but no independent technical-replicate reliability metric for this locus-level signal is reported.
Same cross-sectional rationale as PV-R01-002; no bout exists to anchor a within-organising-window time bin.
HLA-DQB1/HLA-DQA1 are canonical MHC-II antigen-presentation genes in a marker-defined classical-monocyte subset (cMono), a core immune-specific readout (p.5-6).
No repeated-measures or individual-level reproducibility design; not examined for this marker.

Interpreted as 'enhanced antigen presentation capacity' and linked via CellChat to increased MHC-II signaling toward CD4+ T cells (Fig.6D,E), but this is a co-expression/communication-probability inference, not a measured antigen-presentation functional assay (no T-cell activation/proliferation readout, no measured surface HLA-DQ protein level). Discussion explicitly frames the infection-protection link as a proposed interpretation ('may collectively underlie...', p.12), not a tested outcome.
Same single-cohort caveat as PV-R01-006; no independent replication cohort for this signature.
Same rationale as PV-R01-007; requires paired single-cell multiomics assay and bioinformatic pipeline; no cost/turnaround/field-use statement given.

S1 baseline-characteristics table, fig. S2-S3 QC/lipid figures) to recover exact EX/SED n and age/sex breakdown. A related bioRxiv preprint (10.64898/2026.01.13.699221) was not retrieved (see reports table row 'R01-PREPRINT').

eligibility_opinion.rationale: This is a resting cross-sectional comparison of self-reported habitual regular exercisers (EX, n=40) versus sedentary controls (SED, n=46) from the CIMA cohort, with a single fasting morning blood draw per participant and no identifiable single exercise bout, no exercise-cessation timing, and no reported time since last exercise (Methods 'Data source' and 'Blood collection and PBMC separation', p.13-14). It therefore cannot satisfy Core A (needs an identifiable bout with pre/post sampling, contract 2.1-2.2) or Support B (needs >=2 identified bouts with explicit bout-to-sample timing and participant continuity, contract 2.4), and matches the manual's 'resting cross-sectional training studies = background' rule (contract 2.5; 01_protocol/v3_design_contract.txt §2.5).

unresolved_questions: Screening-disposition vocabulary gap: vocabulary_crosswalks.scope_stream.from_screening_disposition only offers EXCLUDE_TA/EXCLUDE_FT mapping to 'excluded OR background if retained for context' - there is no distinct disposition code meaning 'retained as background'. I left reports.screening_decision_reviewer_A/B null rather than guessing between EXCLUDE_FT and an undefined INCLUDE_BACKGROUND value; this needs a team decision/PRE-004 candidate.

Scope of charting for background reports: the manual explicitly states 'how fully to chart background/excluded reports is governed by the manual, and where the manual is unclear it should go into pilot_notes' - it does not specify a concrete stopping rule. Per this task's explicit instruction I charted platforms, donor n per platform and 12 measurement rows plus 14 precision_validation rows; a full formal extraction might reasonably chart much less (or, for full traceability, much more, e.g. every DEG/DAR in tables S3-S4) for a report that sits outside every Core A/B denominator.

Preprint/version linkage: the related bioRxiv preprint (DOI 10.64898/2026.01.13.699221, posted 2026-01) could not be retrieved or read (bioRxiv blocks scripted download per PILOT_README). I created a stub reports row (R01-PREPRINT) for traceability but deliberately did NOT create report_cohort_links/sample_sets/measurements rows for it, since I cannot confirm it shares the same CIMA cohort/dataset as the published Science Advances version. Unclear whether the manual intends a bolder 'merge by default unless disproven' rule versus my conservative 'leave unlinked until confirmed' rule.

Donor-vs-participant distinction for sc-omics sample_sets: I set n_donors = n_participants and donor_count_basis = unique_participants_equivalent for all scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq rows, inferred from table S1 '1.2 sample_omics' (one row per Sample_name, one Sample_name per CIMA participant, no pooling mentioned). I did not independently verify in the raw h5ad/fragment files whether any Sample_name represents more than one donor or a technical repeat; flagged as an assumption rather than a directly reported fact.

Immune relevance of metabolomics/lipidomics/biochemistry arms: the paper's lead quantitative findings (FAO/ketone/antioxidant metabolites, lipid reduction, routine blood biochemistry) are metabolic/cardiometabolic, not immune, and the only immune connection offered is post-hoc Discussion-level pathway narrative (aryl-hydrocarbon-receptor/GABA signaling on immune cells, p.12). Per the manual's own logic for cortisol/CK/lactate/HRV (contract 8.3b), I treated these as non-immune-linked covariates charted for background completeness, but this is a judgment call the manual does not make explicit for metabolomics/lipidomics findings specifically.
